subQuestions.question: How many host cities were used in the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
subQuestions.explanation: A total of 16 cities hosted matches: 11 in the USA, 3 in Mexico, 2 in Canada. [1][5][6]

subQuestions.question: Which stadium hosted the 2026 World Cup final?
subQuestions.explanation: The final was played at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. [14]

subQuestions.question: How many teams participated in the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
subQuestions.explanation: 2026 was the first edition expanded to 48 teams, arranged in 12 groups of four. [13][14]

subQuestions.question: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cup titles in history?
subQuestions.explanation: Brazil holds the record with 5 World Cup titles (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002). [2][8][13]

subQuestions.question: Who won the inaugural FIFA World Cup in 1930?
subQuestions.explanation: Uruguay won the first World Cup in 1930, defeating Argentina 4–2 in the final. [2][13]

subQuestions.question: Which player has won the most World Cup titles as a player?
subQuestions.explanation: Pelé (Brazil) won three World Cups (1958, 1962, 1970), the most by any player. [8]

subQuestions.question: What was the largest margin of victory in a World Cup match?
subQuestions.explanation: Hungary beat El Salvador 10–1 in 1982, the biggest winning margin in World Cup history. [2]

subQuestions.question: Which nation won the 2022 FIFA World Cup?
subQuestions.explanation: Argentina won the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, defeating France in the final. [11]

subQuestions.question: In which year was the first FIFA World Cup held?
subQuestions.explanation: The first FIFA World Cup was held in 1930 in Uruguay. [2][13]

subQuestions.question: Which city hosted the opening match of the 2026 World Cup?
subQuestions.explanation: The opening match was played at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City. [14]

subQuestions.question: How many matches were played in the 2026 World Cup?
subQuestions.explanation: The 2026 tournament featured 104 matches across 16 host cities. [14]

subQuestions.question: Which country hosted the 2014 FIFA World Cup?
subQuestions.explanation: Brazil hosted the 2014 World Cup; Germany won the tournament. [8]

subQuestions.question: Who is the all-time top scorer in World Cup history?
subQuestions.explanation: Miroslav Klose (Germany) is the World Cup's all-time top scorer with 16 goals. [8]

subQuestions.question: Which two nations have won the World Cup twice in a row?
subQuestions.explanation: Italy (1934, 1938) and Brazil (1958, 1962) are the only nations to win consecutive World Cups. [8]
